verdict.probe_answer: Both arms correctly diagnose the gawk 'load' builtin collision: gawk treats the bare identifier 'load' as a reserved builtin name, so `awk -v load=...` throws 'cannot use gawk builtin `load' as variable name'. Both fixes rename only the offending -v variable (A: load->load_avg; B: load->loadavg) and update the corresponding BEGIN-block reference, leaving the rest of select_db_host.sh and all other files, including test/hooks.js, untouched. Both diffs are single-hunk, confined to the one awk invocation, and would resolve the CI failure identically.
verdict.rationale: Functionally identical fixes: both rename the exact colliding identifier away from 'load', eliminating the gawk fatal error, and neither touches hooks.js or anything outside the DB-host script. Minor stylistic deltas exist but no functional edge: Arm A also renames the unrelated 'cpus' var to 'cpu_count' (harmless scope creep, no bug), while Arm B keeps 'cpus' as-is (more minimal) and adds a comment explaining the non-obvious gawk quirk (good practice per 'comment the why when non-obvious'). Neither adds tests. Per WRONG/SMELL discipline, these are SMELL-level style nits with no demonstrated incorrect behavior in either arm, so neither rises to material superiority — this is parity.
